stories.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen3.7-Plus multimodal agent model with 1M-token context

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen3.7-Plus, a closed-source multimodal model that unifies vision and language into an agent foundation, with a 1 million token context window.
Pricing is set at $0.4 to $1.6 per 1M tokens depending on input modality, undercutting prior Qwen tiers, and the model is positioned as a multimodal agent that can operate GUI and CLI interfaces.
Alibaba says Qwen3.7-Plus delivers text-benchmark performance that approaches the company's top-tier Max models.

stories.headline: Bitcoin slides below $67K after Strategy's first BTC sale since 2022 spooks market

key_facts.fact: Bitcoin fell about 8.58% to near $67,206 after Strategy disclosed selling 32 BTC for $2.5 million between May 26-31 at an average of $77,135 per coin
MSTR closed down 9.95% on June 2 and has lost nearly 70% over the past year; market cap fell from above $160B to roughly $48B
Strategy still holds 843,706 BTC at an average cost of $75,699, leaving the position with more than $6 billion in unrealized losses; the 32-coin sale was just 0.0038% of holdings
Proceeds will fund dividend payments on Strategy's STRC perpetual preferred stock; STRC has slipped below its $100 peg
Bitcoin ETFs posted their 10th consecutive day of net outflows on May 29, the longest streak ever; the Crypto Fear & Greed Index hit 23 in 'Extreme Fear' territory
Almost $1.5 billion in crypto liquidations triggered in 24 hours; bitcoin sits more than 42% below its all-time high above $126,000

stories.headline: ChatGPT hits 1B monthly active users in record time; Claude grows 640% YoY to 56M

key_facts.fact: ChatGPT crossed 1 billion global monthly active app users in May, roughly three years after launch, making it the fastest app ever to the milestone per Sensor Tower.
Sensor Tower estimates Claude had 56 million global monthly active app users in Q2-to-date with year-over-year growth of about 640%, versus ChatGPT's 62% YoY growth.
U.S. ChatGPT users who installed Claude in Q1 2026 spent 5% less time on ChatGPT one month after installation compared with their average usage in the prior eight months.
ChatGPT's share of worldwide downloads among six major AI apps tracked by Sensor Tower fell to 47% in Q2 2026-to-date, down from 67% a year earlier.
Sensor Tower noted it took between five and eight years for Google Maps, Chrome, YouTube, Messenger and TikTok to reach 1 billion global monthly active users.

stories.headline: DeepSeek to raise $7.4B in maiden funding from Tencent and CATL at $52-59B valuation

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is set to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.4 billion) in its first funding round from investors including Tencent and CATL.
Post-money valuation is expected between 350 billion and 400 billion yuan, or roughly $52 billion to $59 billion.
Founder Liang Wenfeng is committing 20 billion yuan of personal capital; Tencent is considering 10 billion yuan and CATL 5 billion yuan as the largest external investors.

Fewer than 10 investors are expected to participate, with the round set to close within the next couple of weeks; additional names in talks include IDG Capital, Monolith Capital, NetEase, JD.com and China's national AI fund.

stories.headline: FDA approves Otsuka's sibeprenlimab (Voyxact) for IgA nephropathy after 51% proteinuria cut

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved sibeprenlimab-szsi (Voyxact; Otsuka) to reduce proteinuria in adults with IgA nephropathy, based on interim Phase 3 VISIONARY trial data
Treatment is a 400 mg subcutaneous self-injection via prefilled syringe every 4 weeks at home
VISIONARY trial showed a 51.2% reduction in proteinuria vs placebo at 9 months (p<0.0001); 510 patients enrolled across the cohort
Safety profile showed 76.3% of treated patients experienced any treatment-emergent adverse event vs 84.5% on placebo; serious AE rates were 3.9% vs 5.4%
A confirmatory trial is still needed to determine if sibeprenlimab can slow kidney function decline at 24 months for ongoing approval

stories.headline: GitLab cuts 14% of staff and exits 22 countries in 'agentic era' restructuring

key_facts.fact: GitLab is cutting roughly 350 full-time employees, about 14% of its workforce, and exiting 22 countries to shrink its geographic footprint by about 37%
Restructuring will incur $30-35M in pre-tax charges, primarily severance and termination costs, with about $19M hitting Q2 FY27
Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to $264M, 4 points above guidance; non-GAAP operating income reached $38M at a 14% margin
GitLab Duo Agent Platform contributed more net new ARR in Q1 than Duo Pro and Duo Enterprise combined in any prior quarter, ending Q1 with paid consumption run rate of nearly $20M
CEO Bill Staples framed the layoffs as 'Act Two' restructuring; up to three layers of management will be removed and savings reinvested in R&D and AI tooling
GitLab shares fell 5.83% after the announcement; full-year revenue guidance raised to $1.112-$1.118B

stories.headline: Iran fires missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain; US strikes Qeshm Island in response

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Iran fired ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain on June 2 that failed or were shot down; US responded with strikes on an Iranian ground control station on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
Iran's Fars and Tasnim news agencies reported Tehran stopped communicating with mediators about extending the US-Iran ceasefire; Trump disputed this and said talks were continuing
Brent crude rose above $97 a barrel on June 3, a third consecutive session of gains, as the geopolitical risk premium climbed
Israel kept up strikes on southern Lebanon on June 2 despite a partial truce; Lebanon's Civil Defense said six people were killed in a strike on Marwaniyeh village
Trump told ABC News he expected an agreement to extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within the next week

stories.headline: Marvell shares jump 32% after Jensen Huang calls it the 'next trillion-dollar company' at Computex

key_facts.fact: Marvell shares closed up 32.52% on Tuesday June 2 after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Computex 2026 remarks; intraday gain pushed market cap to about $234B and added more than $45B in market value.
Huang joined Marvell CEO Matt Murphy for a roughly 10-minute on-stage segment during Murphy's Computex 2026 keynote in Taipei on June 2.
Marvell's networking and connectivity chips are critical for AI data centers where computing tasks are distributed across thousands of chips that must share data quickly, Huang said.
Nvidia committed a $2B investment in Marvell earlier this year, part of a broader push into photonics and co-packaged optics partners.
Murphy unveiled Marvell's new T100 Ethernet Switch for AI data centers and pitched co-packaged optics (CPO) as the only path to keep scaling bandwidth while cutting power.
Marvell forecasts custom AI chip business to top $10B in annual revenue by fiscal 2029.

stories.headline: Microsoft launches MAI-Thinking-1 reasoning model, trained from scratch with zero distillation

key_facts.fact: MAI-Thinking-1 is a 35B-active / 1T-total parameter MoE reasoning model with a 256K-token context window, unveiled at Microsoft Build 2026 on June 2.
The model scored 52.8% on SWE-Bench Pro, 97.0% on AIME 2025 and 87.7% on LiveCodeBench v6 according to Microsoft's technical report.
Microsoft trained the model on 30 trillion tokens on 8K GB200 GPUs without distillation from third-party models, excluding AI-generated content from pre-training.
Microsoft says independent human raters on Surge prefer MAI-Thinking-1 to Claude Sonnet 4.6 in blind side-by-side evaluations, and the model matches Claude Opus 4.6 on SWE-Bench Pro.
MAI-Thinking-1 is part of a family of seven new in-house models released at Build, including MAI-Image-2.5 and MAI-Code-1-Flash.
MAI-Image-2.5 debuted at #2 in the Image Edit Arena with a score of 1401, advancing the Pareto frontier per LMArena.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils Majorana 2 topological quantum chip built with AI, eyes commercial quantum machines by 2029

key_facts.fact: Microsoft announced Majorana 2, a next-generation topological quantum chip, at Microsoft Build on June 2, saying it expects commercial quantum systems by 2029.
Microsoft used its Discovery agentic AI platform to help design the new material stack behind Majorana 2.
CEO Satya Nadella said Majorana 1 proved the topological approach physics; Majorana 2 is where the company begins engineering at scale.
Microsoft says the new material stack promises useful quantum computing much sooner than prior roadmaps suggested.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils Project Solara, an Android-based platform for agent-first devices

key_facts.fact: Microsoft introduced Project Solara at Build 2026, an Android-based operating system platform for devices built around AI agents rather than traditional apps.
Microsoft demonstrated two concept devices: an always-on desk device powered by a MediaTek SoC, and a wearable badge-style device.
The platform is built around three principles: enterprise readiness, just-in-time UI that adapts to form factor, and extensibility so customers can bring their own agent.
Pilots with Best Buy, Target and other retailers are planned, framing Solara as Microsoft's bet on a new hardware category in the agent era.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils Surface RTX Spark Dev Box with Nvidia Arm-based RTX Spark and 128GB unified memory

key_facts.fact: Microsoft unveiled the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at Microsoft Build on June 2 — a local-first AI development machine powered by Nvidia's Arm-based RTX Spark with 128GB unified memory and a 100W thermal envelope.
The device is configured and shipped with preinstalled developer tools, presented as turnkey for AI engineers.
Morgan Stanley's checks with PC brands at Computex pegged Nvidia N1X-based AI PC pricing at about US$2,899 for top models, with N1 models lower, per industry leaks circulating during Build week.
Microsoft positioned the Spark Dev Box alongside a broader developer-optimized Windows push: Linux-style Coreutils for Windows, WSL native containers, and an Intelligent Terminal.

stories.headline: French startup Quobly raises €115M Series A to commercialize silicon spin-qubit quantum computers

key_facts.fact: Grenoble-based Quobly raised €115M (~$150M) Series A led by STMicroelectronics, Bpifrance, SEALSQ and Isalt to commercialize silicon spin-qubit quantum computers.

Additional participation from the European Innovation Council, Blast, Air Liquide Venture Capital and existing investor Innovacom; existing shareholders include CEA, CNRS, Quantonation, Supernova Invest.
Quobly plans to ship its first commercial quantum computer by the end of 2026, partner with STMicro on a 100-qubit upgrade in 2027, and target a million-qubit system by 2032.
CEO Maud Vinet framed the round as moving from technology validation to industrial execution.

stories.headline: Drone strike kills seven on bus in Russian-held Donetsk; Russia hits Ukraine with 198 drones overnight

key_facts.fact: Seven people were killed and eleven injured early Wednesday June 3 in a drone attack on a passenger bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-controlled Donetsk, per Kremlin-installed leader Denis Pushilin
Russia launched 198 attack drones against Ukraine overnight June 2-3; Ukrainian air defenses downed 189 of them; impacts recorded at seven locations

Russia downed more than 350 drones overnight on its side, including at least 50 over the Leningrad region, which from Wednesday hosts the St Petersburg International Economic Forum with delegations from 130+ countries

ISW says Russia's June 2 strike (656 drones + 73 missiles) was designed to exploit Ukrainian Patriot missile shortages and divert attention from setbacks; Russia used cluster munitions and double-tap strikes on emergency responders
Zelensky warned that intelligence suggests Russia could launch a new large-scale attack on the night of June 3

organizations: Institute for the Study of War

stories.headline: SoftBank in early talks to anchor $800M Agile Robots round as humanoid race goes capital-intensive

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is in early discussions to anchor an $800M round for Munich-based Agile Robots, Bloomberg reported June 2.
If completed, the round would put Agile Robots in the same capital tier as the best-funded humanoid and physical-AI peers; SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 previously led Agile's $220M Series C in 2021.
The talks fit SoftBank's broader robotics pivot: a $5.375B acquisition of ABB Robotics (Oct 2025) and plans for a standalone AI/robotics company called Roze targeting a $100B valuation.
SoftBank tapped Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Mizuho and Morgan Stanley on May 26 to prep a US IPO for Roze.

stories.headline: SpaceX targets record $75B IPO at $135 per share, $1.75T valuation

key_facts.fact: SpaceX plans to sell 555.6 million shares at $135 each to raise $75 billion, an unusual move that fixes a price before the investor roadshow
Target valuation is $1.75 trillion in what would be the largest IPO in history; the offering is structured as all-primary with no insider sales
Roadshow begins Thursday June 4; SpaceX aims to debut on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX as early as June 12
Musk will be required to hold his SpaceX shares for 366 days after the IPO under a lockup; greenshoe option set at 15%
Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities, Citigroup and JPMorgan are joint book-running managers

stories.headline: AI music startup Suno raises $400M at $5.4B valuation, led by Bond Capital

key_facts.fact: Suno raised $400 million at a $5.4 billion valuation, with Bond Capital leading the round alongside IVP, Forerunner and Union Square Ventures; existing backers Lightspeed and Menlo Ventures also participated.
The valuation more than doubled from the $2.45 billion mark set in Suno's November 2025 Series C, which raised $250 million.
Suno passed 2 million paid subscribers in February 2026 and is tracking toward $300 million in annual revenue.
The startup employs about 200 people and plans to grow headcount by up to 70% before year-end, per co-founder and CEO Mikey Shulman.

stories.headline: Trump signs scaled-back AI executive order focused on cybersecurity and voluntary review

key_facts.fact: President Trump signed an executive order on June 2, 2026 establishing a voluntary framework for evaluating advanced AI models with significant cybersecurity capabilities, rejecting mandatory licensing or preclearance.
The order shortens the federal pre-deployment review window for covered frontier models from 90 days in earlier drafts to up to 30 days.
The order directs Treasury, NSA and CISA to develop classified benchmarks to assess advanced cyber capabilities of AI systems and identify 'covered frontier models'.
It also establishes an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse coordinating vulnerability scanning and patching with industry and critical infrastructure operators in voluntary collaboration.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman publicly backed the order, saying it 'gets the balance right' between developing the best models and getting cyber tools into defenders' hands.

stories.headline: US sanctions Nobitex and three other Iranian crypto exchanges over IRGC links

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury's OFAC designated Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex on June 2 for facilitating terrorist financing and sanctions evasion
Treasury alleges Nobitex processed more than 50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025 and facilitated IRGC-linked transactions including ransomware payments
Nobitex handled roughly $5 billion in transactions from 2025 to March 2026, per TRM Labs

Treasury also sanctioned Nobitex's three co-founders and current CEO; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his department has seized roughly $1 billion in crypto from Iranian wallets since the war began
Treasury alleges Nobitex helped Iran move assets out of the country after US bombing began and aided the Central Bank of Iran in accessing stablecoins to prop up the rial

stories.headline: Vingroup commits $12.75M to Vinmotion USA humanoid robotics R&D arm

key_facts.fact: Vingroup's board approved a $12.75M investment in Vinmotion USA, Inc., a humanoid robot and AI research subsidiary, with the resolution dated May 29 and disclosure on June 2.
Plans include building a US R&D center to attract global talent and partner with universities, research institutes and tech firms.
Vinmotion USA is being acquired from VinMotion General Purpose Humanoid Robots Application, Development and Research JSC, a Vingroup subsidiary spun up to focus on general-purpose humanoid robots.

organizations: VinMotion General Purpose Humanoid Robots Application, Development and Research JSC

stories.headline: ZutaCore raises $100M Series C at ~$600M valuation for direct-to-chip AI data center cooling

key_facts.fact: Israeli direct-to-chip liquid cooling startup ZutaCore closed a $100M Series C led by Mitsubishi Electric, Carrier and Samsung Ventures, announced on June 2.
The round values ZutaCore at about $600M and brings total funding to roughly $200M since founding, per Calcalist.
ZutaCore says its waterless two-phase cooling has been deployed at over 75 sites in North America, Europe and Asia, with partnerships across semiconductor and computing firms.
Capital will go to scaling commercial sales and expanding capacity to meet AI/HPC infrastructure demand.
